item_format: child sees two side-by-side patterns and taps a smiley (same) or frowny (different) face as fast as possible for about 90 seconds
cognitive_process: perceptual comparison speed plus sustained attention (a simple choice reaction time)
engagement_affordance: non-verbal smiley/frowny taps already feel game-like for young children; add a countdown and combo meter, but score accuracy and consistency (not peak speed) so it never rewards impulsive tapping
adaptivity_fit: high - stimuli vary by color or add/remove an element; difficulty via similarity and item count; speed is a continuous measure, less classic CAT
tail_discrimination: low - items are deliberately easy with errors minimized, so it captures speed not ceiling ability; weak at separating the gifted tail
coachability_bias_risk: moderate-to-large practice effect (about 5.5 points over one week in norming); touchscreen/motor latency and attention/ADHD strongly move scores
advantage_vs_cogat: weak as a STANDALONE gifted signal; its value is collateral evidence of engagement/effort and response CONSISTENCY (slowest-response/lapse rate), which tracks ability better than peak speed; CogAT gives no timing or process data
source_name: NIH Toolbox Pattern Comparison Processing Speed Test
reuse_note: describe_only - characterize the paradigm and build our own stimuli; do not copy Toolbox content

item_format: decide if two simple figures are the same or different when they differ by one feature (a color or an added dot) and tap YES or NO quickly
cognitive_process: perceptual discrimination speed
engagement_affordance: quick same/different rounds suit a fast-paced card-flip mini-game; keep a streak bonus for accurate calls rather than raw speed
adaptivity_fit: high - trivially templated; difficulty scales with feature similarity and number of features
tail_discrimination: low-to-med - easy ceiling; only the hardest similarity levels show any high-end spread
coachability_bias_risk: large practice effects; strategy and familiarity transfer quickly; device latency confounds timing
advantage_vs_cogat: as a standalone gifted signal it is weak; useful mainly as an engagement/effort check and for response consistency; CogAT captures reasoning but no processing efficiency
source_name: Salthouse Pattern Comparison (UT Dallas Park Aging Mind Lab)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - classic public research paradigm; generate our own figure pairs

item_format: decide whether two number strings (3, 6, or 9 digits) are identical or different and complete as many as possible in 45 seconds per set
cognitive_process: perceptual comparison speed with a light working-memory load as string length grows
engagement_affordance: length tiers (3/6/9 digits) map naturally onto level-ups; reward correct calls per minute, not fastest single tap
adaptivity_fit: high - string length and digit similarity give clean difficulty knobs; auto-generated
tail_discrimination: low-to-med - longer strings add a small working-memory demand that gives slightly more high-end spread than pure pattern matching
coachability_bias_risk: practice and chunking strategies inflate scores; numeracy familiarity and device speed confound
advantage_vs_cogat: weak alone; the added working-memory element is a minor edge, but the honest value is consistency/effort evidence, not peak speed; CogAT has no speeded component
source_name: Salthouse and Babcock Number/Pattern Comparison (UT Dallas Park Aging Mind Lab)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - public research paradigm; build our own digit strings

item_format: same/not-same judgement on two visual patterns that may differ by color, by adding/removing an element, or (for older children) one-versus-many, using yes/no buttons
cognitive_process: choice reaction time over perceptual comparison
engagement_affordance: the one-versus-many dimension can become a distinct game mode; still score correct-per-90s and flag impulsive wrong-fast responses
adaptivity_fit: high - three difficulty dimensions already built into the paradigm; continuous speed score
tail_discrimination: low - by construction items stay easy to isolate speed; poor ceiling for gifted screening
coachability_bias_risk: documented practice effect; motor/device and attention confounds; motivation-sensitive
advantage_vs_cogat: weak standalone; best used as collateral evidence and a consistency metric; CogAT offers no processing-speed index at all
source_name: NIH Toolbox Pattern Comparison Processing Speed Test (LOINC 84436-5)
reuse_note: describe_only - characterize the paradigm; do not reproduce Toolbox items

item_format: in each row of six numbers, find and mark the two that are identical, completing as many rows as possible within a 3-minute limit (early rows use small numbers/shapes for young children)
cognitive_process: perceptual speed / number-pattern matching
engagement_affordance: row-by-row matching maps to a timed find-the-twins board; use touch selection and per-row feedback, rewarding accuracy over raw pace
adaptivity_fit: med-to-high - rows are easily generated, but the fixed 3-minute paper format is less naturally adaptive
tail_discrimination: low - a perceptual-speed test, not a reasoning test; ceilings quickly and does not stretch the gifted tail
coachability_bias_risk: practice effects; fine-motor and visual-tracking demands add construct-irrelevant variance for the youngest children
advantage_vs_cogat: weak as a gifted signal; describe the format only; value is process/effort data CogAT lacks, not tail discrimination
source_name: Woodcock-Johnson IV Number-Pattern Matching (formerly Visual Matching) [proprietary]
reuse_note: describe_only - do not reproduce secure WJ items; build an original number-matching template

item_format: locate and draw a line through the two identical letter clusters in a row of six, working as fast as possible for 3 minutes (orthographic perceptual speed)
cognitive_process: perceptual speed plus orthographic pattern recognition
engagement_affordance: letter-cluster matching suits a timed word-arcade; touch-select the twin clusters, streak bonus for accuracy
adaptivity_fit: high - letter clusters are cheap to template and can be tuned for similarity
tail_discrimination: low - measures speed of visual symbol discrimination, not reasoning; weak high-end spread
coachability_bias_risk: reading fluency and orthographic familiarity confound it; practice effects; disadvantages emerging/EL readers
advantage_vs_cogat: weak standalone; describe only; the orthographic angle is reading-linked, not a clean gifted signal; keep as collateral evidence
source_name: Woodcock-Johnson IV Letter-Pattern Matching [proprietary]
reuse_note: describe_only - do not reproduce WJ content; create an original letter-cluster task

item_format: scan a search group of symbols and mark whether either target symbol is present, moving row by row against the clock
cognitive_process: visual scanning, discrimination and decision speed
engagement_affordance: target-present decisions gamify as a fast is-it-here scanner; on touch, reward correct calls and penalize false alarms to curb impulsive speed
adaptivity_fit: high - templated symbol arrays; density and target-distractor similarity control difficulty
tail_discrimination: low - a classic speed subtest; gifted children can even underperform slightly relative to reasoning, so it does not mark the tail
coachability_bias_risk: large practice effects; graphomotor/device speed confounds; attention-sensitive
advantage_vs_cogat: weak alone; describe the type only; its worth is process data and an engagement check, not high-end discrimination
source_name: WISC-V Symbol Search (Pearson) [proprietary]
reuse_note: describe_only - do not reproduce secure Wechsler content; build an original target-present scanner

item_format: look at one target shape, then tap YES if it appears in the row of shapes and NO if it does not, going as fast as you can
cognitive_process: visual search and target detection speed
engagement_affordance: simple yes/no scanning is easy to gamify with a countdown and cheerful streaks; keep set sizes tiny for the youngest and reward correct calls
adaptivity_fit: high - open-source visual search templates; set size and similarity scale difficulty
tail_discrimination: low - detection speed alone does not separate high-ability preschoolers
coachability_bias_risk: fast practice gains; motor/device latency dominates at this age; attention-driven
advantage_vs_cogat: weak standalone; useful only as engagement/effort and consistency evidence; CogAT is not administered this young in this form
source_name: PEBL Test Battery - Visual Search (open source)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - GPL library; reuse or modify the visual-search task

item_format: arcade spot-the-target: tap every shape that matches the target as it slides across the screen before the timer runs out
cognitive_process: visual search plus sustained attention and motor speed
engagement_affordance: the most gamifiable speed format - arcade motion, countdown, combo meter; the combo must break on false taps so it rewards controlled, not impulsive, speed
adaptivity_fit: high - spawn rate, target density and similarity are live difficulty dials; speed is continuous
tail_discrimination: low - fun but weak for the tail; peak taps-per-second is heavily motor/device bound
coachability_bias_risk: very large practice/skill effects; device frame-rate and touch latency confound; strongly attention/impulsivity driven
advantage_vs_cogat: weak as a gifted signal; its real value is keeping effort high and yielding a consistency/impulsivity read; CogAT provides no engagement telemetry
source_name: PEBL Test Battery (open-source cognitive tasks)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - GPL v2; reuse and restyle the search task as an arcade layer

item_format: visual search: find the target among distractors; response time and accuracy scale with set size and target-distractor similarity
cognitive_process: serial/parallel visual search efficiency
engagement_affordance: set-size levels give a natural difficulty ladder for a scanner game; log accuracy and RT variability, not just the fastest hit
adaptivity_fit: high - browser-based, fully parameterized, embeddable; clones cheaply
tail_discrimination: low-to-med - the search slope (RT vs set size) is a slightly more ability-linked index than raw speed
coachability_bias_risk: practice effects; device latency; attention-dependent; speed-accuracy tradeoff must be controlled
advantage_vs_cogat: weak alone; the search slope and consistency add modest process information CogAT lacks; not a tail discriminator by itself
source_name: PsyToolkit Experiment Library (visual search)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - copy and modify library experiments for our own study

item_format: cross out or tap every target letter (for example every letter d) hidden in rows of similar letters, as fast and accurately as possible
cognitive_process: selective attention, visual scanning and target cancellation speed
engagement_affordance: row-clearing cancellation feels like a timed find-them-all sweep; show a live accuracy meter so kids optimize hits minus false alarms, not raw pace
adaptivity_fit: high - target/distractor similarity and density are easy dials; auto-generated grids
tail_discrimination: low - cancellation indexes attention/speed, not reasoning; poor high-end separation
coachability_bias_risk: practice effects; strongly attention/impulsivity and motivation driven; motor/device speed confounds
advantage_vs_cogat: weak standalone; its worth is a sustained-attention/effort read and false-alarm (impulsivity) signal; CogAT captures none of this
source_name: Letter Cancellation Test (Millisecond Test Library, public paradigm)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - the LCT is a public paradigm (the d2 is the commercial variant); build our own grids

item_format: scan 14 timed rows and mark every letter d that carries exactly two marks while ignoring d's with other numbers of marks and all p's
cognitive_process: selective and sustained attention, concentration, visual scanning speed
engagement_affordance: the tight target rule suits a precision-cancellation game; score concentration performance (hits minus false alarms) so speed alone cannot win
adaptivity_fit: med - the fixed timed-row structure is standardized; our own variant could parameterize similarity/density
tail_discrimination: low - designed for attention/concentration, not gifted reasoning; weak tail spread
coachability_bias_risk: practice effects; attention/ADHD sensitive; the fine target discrimination adds visual load; secular score gains reported
advantage_vs_cogat: weak standalone; describe only; useful as an attention/effort and impulsivity check, not for identifying the gifted tail
source_name: d2 Test of Attention (Brickenkamp) [proprietary]
reuse_note: describe_only - do not reproduce d2 content; build an original two-mark cancellation task

item_format: scan one random and one structured array of pictures and mark the target objects (for example the animals) within a time limit
cognitive_process: visual selective attention and scanning speed
engagement_affordance: picture targets make a friendly tap-all-the-animals sweep; the random-vs-structured contrast can be two levels; reward accuracy over pace
adaptivity_fit: high - picture sets and density template easily; continuous speed score
tail_discrimination: low - a speed/attention subtest; does not stretch the gifted tail
coachability_bias_risk: practice effects; motor/device speed and attention confounds; young-child motivation swings
advantage_vs_cogat: weak standalone; describe only; value is engagement/attention evidence, not tail discrimination
source_name: WISC-V Cancellation subtest (Pearson) [proprietary]
reuse_note: describe_only - do not reproduce Wechsler content; build an original picture-cancellation sweep

item_format: locate and circle a specific repeated pair of pictures as quickly as possible for 3 minutes, ignoring all other pictures
cognitive_process: processing speed with interference control and sustained attention (an executive-tinged speed task)
engagement_affordance: hunting a specific pair suits a timed find-the-combo game; the inhibition demand adds interest; still score hits minus false alarms
adaptivity_fit: med-to-high - pair templates generate cheaply; the fixed 3-minute format is less adaptive out of the box
tail_discrimination: low-to-med - the added inhibition/interference control gives marginally more high-end variance than pure cancellation
coachability_bias_risk: practice effects; attention and inhibition sensitive; visual layout can disadvantage some children
advantage_vs_cogat: weak alone; describe only; the inhibition component is a small edge, but treat it as collateral executive/effort evidence, not a gifted marker
source_name: Woodcock-Johnson IV Pair Cancellation [proprietary]
reuse_note: describe_only - do not reproduce WJ content; design an original repeated-pair cancellation

item_format: mobile cancellation: tap all targets in each row before it advances; the app auto-scores hits, false alarms and a concentration-performance index
cognitive_process: selective and sustained attention with visual scanning speed
engagement_affordance: built for phones/tablets with auto-advancing rows and instant feedback; naturally game-like; expose the concentration score so accuracy, not raw speed, is the goal
adaptivity_fit: high - designed for participant devices with automated scoring; density/similarity parameterizable
tail_discrimination: low - an attention/speed measure; weak for the gifted tail even with clean scoring
coachability_bias_risk: practice effects; device and touch-latency variance; attention/impulsivity driven
advantage_vs_cogat: weak standalone; strong as an engagement/attention check and false-alarm (impulsivity) read on the child's own device; CogAT offers none of this
source_name: UCancellation - a mobile measure of selective attention (open)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - freely accessible open measure; reimplement the paradigm

item_format: tap every apple hidden among other fruits across the screen as fast as you can (a child-friendly cancellation sweep)
cognitive_process: visual selective attention and target cancellation
engagement_affordance: a warm, low-reading harvest-the-apples sweep; combo builds on correct taps and breaks on wrong fruit to discourage frantic tapping
adaptivity_fit: high - swap picture themes; density and distractor similarity scale difficulty
tail_discrimination: low - attention/speed only; not a gifted-tail discriminator
coachability_bias_risk: large practice gains; motor/device latency dominates for young kids; attention-driven
advantage_vs_cogat: weak standalone; value is engagement/effort and impulsivity evidence for young children CogAT cannot test this way
source_name: Target Cancellation paradigm (Millisecond Test Library, public)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - public cancellation paradigm; create our own picture themes

item_format: using a key that pairs each digit 1-9 with a symbol, write the symbol under each digit as fast as possible for 90-120 seconds
cognitive_process: visual scanning, associative learning and graphomotor/response speed
engagement_affordance: the key-lookup loop gamifies as a timed decode-the-message level; as pairs are learned it speeds up, giving a satisfying curve; score correct matches, not frantic guesses
adaptivity_fit: high - key size, symbol set and time limit are simple dials; endlessly regenerable
tail_discrimination: low - a canonical speed test; gifted children may even score modestly relative to reasoning; poor tail marker
coachability_bias_risk: large practice/learning effects (the key gets memorized); graphomotor and device speed confound; attention-sensitive
advantage_vs_cogat: weak standalone; the incidental associative-learning aspect is interesting collateral, but treat speed as effort/consistency evidence only; CogAT has no such process data
source_name: Digit Symbol Substitution Test (public-domain paradigm; Otis 1918 / Thorndike 1919)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - century-old public paradigm; build our own key and symbols

item_format: copy the symbol that corresponds to each geometric shape or number using a printed key, working as fast as possible within the time limit
cognitive_process: associative memory, visual scanning and graphomotor speed
engagement_affordance: the same decode-the-key loop as generic coding; on tablet it removes handwriting; reward correct decodes and consistency, not raw pace
adaptivity_fit: high - the format templates trivially in an original design (do not reuse Wechsler symbols)
tail_discrimination: low - a speed subtest that does not separate the gifted tail; may underrepresent able but deliberate children
coachability_bias_risk: large practice effects; graphomotor demand penalizes fine-motor delays; device/handwriting confounds
advantage_vs_cogat: weak standalone; describe only; keep as process/effort evidence, not a gifted signal
source_name: WISC-V Coding (Pearson Q-interactive Processing Speed technical report) [proprietary]
reuse_note: describe_only - do not reproduce Wechsler symbols/keys; build an original coding task

item_format: on-screen DSST: a 1-9 symbol key sits at the top and the child taps the symbol matching each presented digit; score is correct matches in 120 seconds
cognitive_process: perceptual matching speed with associative learning
engagement_affordance: a ready decode game; the improving speed as pairs are learned is intrinsically motivating; display accuracy so it does not devolve into mashing
adaptivity_fit: high - open script; change symbols, key length, and duration; embeddable in a survey
tail_discrimination: low - standard speed measure; weak high-end spread
coachability_bias_risk: strong practice/memorization effects; device input latency; attention-sensitive
advantage_vs_cogat: weak standalone; use for engagement and response consistency; CogAT gives no speeded/process signal
source_name: PsyToolkit - Digit Symbol Substitution Test (open)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - download and modify the PsyToolkit script

item_format: match each picture (star, cat, sun) to its partner shape using a small two-row key, tapping as many correct pairs as possible before time runs out
cognitive_process: symbol-pair association and matching speed (a pre-numeric coding analog)
engagement_affordance: a picture-based decode game for pre-readers; keep the key tiny (4-6 pairs) and reward accurate matches with cheerful streaks
adaptivity_fit: high - key size and picture similarity scale difficulty; regenerable themes
tail_discrimination: low - speed/association only; does not separate high-ability preschoolers
coachability_bias_risk: rapid learning of a small key; motor/device latency dominates; attention-driven
advantage_vs_cogat: weak standalone; value is engagement/effort and consistency at an age CogAT cannot reach in this format
source_name: Digit/Symbol Substitution paradigm (public; picture-coding analog of WISC Coding A)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - public paradigm; design an original picture key

item_format: given a symbol-digit key, the child says aloud the digit that matches each symbol as fast as possible (a motor-reduced, spoken coding task)
cognitive_process: perceptual matching speed with verbal output, minimizing graphomotor load
engagement_affordance: spoken responses suit a voice-driven decode round; removing handwriting reduces motor confounds; capture voice-onset consistency, not just count
adaptivity_fit: med-to-high - needs speech capture/scoring, but the key and symbols template easily
tail_discrimination: low - still a speed measure; removing motor load cleans it a little but does not create tail spread
coachability_bias_risk: practice/memorization effects remain; expressive-language and articulation speed confound; attention-sensitive
advantage_vs_cogat: weak standalone; the motor-reduced design is a fairness advantage over graphomotor coding, but keep it as collateral evidence; CogAT has no oral-speed measure
source_name: NIH Toolbox Oral Symbol Digit Test (Administrator Manual)
reuse_note: describe_only - characterize the oral coding paradigm; build our own key

item_format: name aloud, left to right, a grid of familiar repeated objects (ball, dog, star) as fast as possible; score is total naming time and errors
cognitive_process: rapid lexical retrieval, serial visual scanning and articulation speed
engagement_affordance: naming a friendly picture grid suits a read-aloud race with a gentle timer; capture voice onsets and pauses rather than gamifying pure speed
adaptivity_fit: med - grids template easily, but scoring needs speech timing; not classic CAT
tail_discrimination: low-to-med - RAN predicts reading fluency strongly but is not a broad giftedness marker; more diagnostic of fluency/risk than of the high tail
coachability_bias_risk: notably HARD to coach - a training study found no reliable transfer to RAN or reading; still affected by vocabulary familiarity, language and articulation speed
advantage_vs_cogat: weak as a general gifted signal but genuinely LESS coachable than most speed tasks and a strong early-literacy/fluency predictor CogAT ignores; best as a less-coachable collateral measure (serves H4)
source_name: Norton and Wolf - What educators need to know about RAN
reuse_note: adapt_ok - RAN is a public research paradigm; normed kits (CTOPP, RAN/RAS) are proprietary, so build our own grids

item_format: name a grid of repeated color patches (red, blue, green, black) as fast as possible; a pre-literacy naming-speed measure for children who do not yet know letters
cognitive_process: rapid retrieval of over-learned names with serial scanning
engagement_affordance: a color-calling race with a soft timer; emphasize smooth continuous naming, capturing pauses/lapses rather than peak speed
adaptivity_fit: med - simple to generate; speech-timing scoring required
tail_discrimination: low - color RAN is a fluency/risk indicator, not a gifted-tail discriminator
coachability_bias_risk: resistant to direct coaching; still influenced by color-word familiarity and language background
advantage_vs_cogat: weak for the tail but less coachable and an early-fluency predictor CogAT omits; keep as collateral, equity-relevant evidence
source_name: Reading Rockets - Rapid automatized naming (Shanahan on Literacy)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - public paradigm; build our own color grids

item_format: name a grid of repeated letters (rapid letter naming) as fast as possible; the alphanumeric RAN most strongly linked to reading fluency
cognitive_process: rapid letter-name retrieval, serial scanning and articulation
engagement_affordance: a letter-naming speed run; keep it a low-pressure race and log lapse pauses, since consistency (not top speed) carries the signal
adaptivity_fit: med - trivially generated grids; needs speech-onset scoring
tail_discrimination: low-to-med - alphanumeric RAN is the strongest reading-fluency predictor of the RAN family but still not a broad giftedness marker
coachability_bias_risk: hard to coach directly; confounded by letter familiarity, orthographic exposure and language background
advantage_vs_cogat: weak for the gifted tail but a robust, less-coachable fluency predictor CogAT lacks; useful collateral for a broader profile (H1/H4)
source_name: Rapid Automatized Naming and Word Reading Fluency (PMC pilot eye-tracking study)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - public paradigm; construct our own letter grids

item_format: name a grid of repeated digits (rapid digit naming) as fast as possible; score is completion time and errors
cognitive_process: rapid digit-name retrieval with serial scanning
engagement_affordance: a number-calling race; capture rhythm and pauses; reward smooth continuous naming rather than a single fast burst
adaptivity_fit: med - easy grids; speech-timing scoring needed
tail_discrimination: low-to-med - alphanumeric RAN predicts fluency well but is not a general high-ability marker
coachability_bias_risk: resistant to coaching; confounded by number familiarity and articulation speed
advantage_vs_cogat: weak for the tail; a less-coachable, fluency-linked collateral measure CogAT does not capture
source_name: Rapid Automatized Naming and Word Reading Fluency (PMC pilot eye-tracking study)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - public paradigm; build our own digit grids

item_format: contrast serial (full-grid) rapid naming, which requires sustained scanning and eye-movements, against discrete single-item naming; the serial format is far more ability/reading linked
cognitive_process: serial rapid retrieval with sustained scanning versus isolated retrieval
engagement_affordance: use the serial grid, not single-item flashcards, so the sustained-scanning demand (the ability-linked part) is preserved; log lapse frequency across the grid
adaptivity_fit: med - grids generate cheaply; scoring needs speech timing
tail_discrimination: low-to-med - serial RAN carries the reading/fluency signal; discrete naming is weaker still
coachability_bias_risk: RAN broadly resists coaching; the serial format additionally taxes attention, so effort matters
advantage_vs_cogat: weak for the tail, but the serial-vs-discrete distinction is a design lesson: preserve continuous scanning to retain the less-coachable fluency signal CogAT misses
source_name: Norton and Wolf - What educators need to know about RAN
reuse_note: describe_only - implement serial grids ourselves; do not use proprietary RAN kits

item_format: press the button the instant a single shape or light appears; repeated over many trials; record mean and (critically) the variability of response time
cognitive_process: stimulus detection and motor response speed
engagement_affordance: a ready-set-go tap game; use catch trials so jumping the gun is penalized, teaching controlled rather than impulsive speed
adaptivity_fit: low-to-med - little to make harder; mainly repeat trials for a stable estimate; not classic CAT
tail_discrimination: low - mean simple RT barely relates to ability; the useful part is intra-individual variability, not speed
coachability_bias_risk: practice effects; heavily device/touch-latency bound; anticipation and attention lapses dominate at this age
advantage_vs_cogat: weak alone; its honest value is that RT variability/lapses (not fast taps) track ability, and it gives an effort/attention read CogAT cannot
source_name: Deary-Liewald reaction time task (PsyToolkit)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - open task; capture the full RT distribution, not just the mean

item_format: standardized simple reaction time: one stimulus, one response, many trials; the task records mean RT and, importantly, the standard deviation of RT
cognitive_process: basic stimulus-response speed and its consistency
engagement_affordance: minimal but gamifiable as a reflex meter; surface consistency (steadiness) as the headline score, not the single fastest tap
adaptivity_fit: low-to-med - difficulty is fixed; precision comes from trial count
tail_discrimination: low - mean simple RT is a weak correlate of intelligence; RT SD is the more ability-linked index
coachability_bias_risk: practice and device latency; anticipation and lapses; motivation-sensitive
advantage_vs_cogat: weak standalone; the standardized RT distribution (especially variability) is process data CogAT lacks; still not a tail discriminator
source_name: Deary-Liewald reaction time task (PsyToolkit; Deary, Liewald and Nissan 2011)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - open, standardized task; reuse with our own trial counts

item_format: arcade whack-it: tap the critter the moment it pops up; combo rewards fast AND correct hits while tapping an empty hole breaks the combo
cognitive_process: detection and motor response speed with response inhibition on empty targets
engagement_affordance: maximally fun and low-reading; the empty-hole penalty is the key design guard against rewarding impulsive fast-but-wrong tapping
adaptivity_fit: med - pop-up rate and dwell time scale difficulty; speed is continuous
tail_discrimination: low - a reflex/attention game; peak speed is motor/device bound and does not mark the tail
coachability_bias_risk: very large skill/practice effects; device frame-rate and touch latency; strongly impulsivity/attention driven
advantage_vs_cogat: weak as a gifted signal; excels at sustaining effort and yielding an impulsivity/consistency read; CogAT provides no such behavioral telemetry
source_name: PEBL Test Battery (open-source reaction-time tasks)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - GPL library; wrap the RT task in an arcade layer with a false-tap penalty

cognitive_process: stimulus-response mapping and decision speed under choice load
engagement_affordance: a four-lane reflex game; report accuracy and consistency alongside speed so children do not trade accuracy for a faster clock
adaptivity_fit: med-to-high - number of alternatives and pacing scale difficulty; continuous score
tail_discrimination: low-to-med - choice RT relates to intelligence a bit more than simple RT, but the correlation is modest and mostly carried by consistency
coachability_bias_risk: practice effects; device latency; speed-accuracy tradeoff; attention-sensitive
advantage_vs_cogat: weak alone; the choice-load slope and RT consistency add modest process signal CogAT lacks; not a standalone gifted marker
source_name: Deary-Liewald four-choice reaction time task (PsyToolkit)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - open task; reuse the choice block

item_format: tap the left or the right target depending on which side a friendly animal appears; a fast, low-reading two-choice reaction task
cognitive_process: simple decision and response-selection speed
engagement_affordance: a left/right catch game; short blocks with feedback; reward steady correct responses and flag anticipatory taps
adaptivity_fit: med - two choices with pacing dials; speed continuous
tail_discrimination: low - two-choice RT is a weak ability correlate at this age; motor/attention dominated
coachability_bias_risk: practice effects; device latency; young-child attention and impulsivity swings
advantage_vs_cogat: weak standalone; useful as an engagement/effort and consistency read for pre-readers CogAT cannot assess this way
source_name: Deary-Liewald reaction time task (PsyToolkit)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - open task; simplify to two choices for young children

item_format: choice reaction time across 1, 2, 4 and 8 alternatives; the slope of RT against log2(number of choices) indexes information-processing rate
cognitive_process: information-processing rate under increasing choice/decision load
engagement_affordance: escalating-lane levels naturally gamify the choice-load ladder; still headline accuracy and consistency, not raw speed
adaptivity_fit: high - number of alternatives is a clean, principled difficulty parameter
tail_discrimination: low-to-med - the Hick slope correlates with intelligence but modestly; individual variability still dominates the signal
coachability_bias_risk: practice effects; device latency; speed-accuracy tradeoff; attention-dependent
advantage_vs_cogat: weak alone; a principled processing-rate slope is more interpretable process data than a single speed score, but it is not a tail discriminator; keep as collateral
source_name: Deary-Liewald task implementing the Hick/Jensen choice-RT paradigm (PsyToolkit)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - open task; vary the number of alternatives to recover the Hick slope

item_format: open-source choice reaction time task with a configurable number of alternatives and inter-stimulus interval
cognitive_process: decision and response-selection speed and its consistency
engagement_affordance: fully configurable, so it can be reskinned per age as a reflex/decision game; expose consistency and accuracy as primary scores
adaptivity_fit: high - open parameters (alternatives, ISI, blocks); embeddable and clonable
tail_discrimination: low - choice RT is a weak standalone ability index; the consistency/lapse component is the informative part
coachability_bias_risk: practice effects; device latency; speed-accuracy tradeoff; attention-driven
advantage_vs_cogat: weak standalone; open telemetry (the full RT distribution) is process/effort data CogAT lacks; not a gifted marker by itself
source_name: PEBL Test Battery (open-source choice reaction time)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - GPL v2; reuse and configure the choice-RT task

item_format: two vertical lines of different length joined by a bar (a Pi-figure) flash briefly and are then masked; report which side (left or right) was longer; inspection time is the exposure needed to reach a threshold accuracy
cognitive_process: speed of perceptual intake/discrimination, largely free of motor speed
engagement_affordance: the flash-then-answer format suits an unspeeded what-did-you-see game; because the response is untimed, it resists reward-for-fast-tapping by design
adaptivity_fit: high - stimulus exposure duration is a precise, staircaseable difficulty parameter (naturally adaptive)
tail_discrimination: low-to-med - inspection time correlates about 0.3-0.5 with IQ (stronger in the lower range), so it is a modest, not strong, high-tail discriminator
coachability_bias_risk: practice effects; crucially, some people exploit apparent-motion/visual cues and illusions, inflating scores; needs good masking to stay valid
advantage_vs_cogat: weak-to-moderate standalone; its motor-free design avoids the device/graphomotor confounds of tap tasks, a genuine fairness edge; still treat as collateral evidence, not a gifted cutoff
source_name: Inspection time (research paradigm overview)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - classic public paradigm; build our own Pi-figure and mask

item_format: two towers flash on screen then vanish behind a mask; the child taps the taller tower afterward at their leisure; accuracy at very short exposures is the score
cognitive_process: brief perceptual intake and magnitude discrimination without time pressure on the response
engagement_affordance: a peekaboo which-was-taller game; the unspeeded response means fast tapping earns nothing, so it naturally avoids the impulsivity trap
adaptivity_fit: high - exposure duration staircases difficulty precisely per child
tail_discrimination: low-to-med - motor-free perceptual speed with a modest IQ link; better as a clean process index than a tail cutoff
coachability_bias_risk: practice effects; children may use motion/afterimage cues unless masking is strong; attention still matters
advantage_vs_cogat: weak-to-moderate; motor-free and unspeeded-response, so it is fairer to slow-tapping or motor-delayed able children than speeded taps; keep as collateral
source_name: How Do People Perform an Inspection Time Task? (Journal of Cognition)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - public paradigm; build a child-friendly two-tower version with strong masking

item_format: backward-masked brief discrimination (which of two stimuli was longer or different) presented as a motor-free index of perceptual intake speed
cognitive_process: rate of early perceptual information intake
engagement_affordance: flash-and-recall rounds keep it game-like without rewarding motor speed; vary exposure to create difficulty tiers rather than speeding the response
adaptivity_fit: high - the exposure-duration staircase is inherently adaptive and precise
tail_discrimination: low-to-med - a modest IQ correlate; strategy use and illusions can inflate it, so it is not a clean gifted-tail cutoff
coachability_bias_risk: practice and strategy effects (cue exploitation) are the main threats; robust masking and catch trials are required
advantage_vs_cogat: weak-to-moderate standalone; the value is a motor/device-free perceptual-speed read that CogAT lacks; still collateral, not decisive
source_name: How Do People Perform an Inspection Time Task? (Journal of Cognition)
reuse_note: describe_only - characterize the paradigm; implement our own masked stimuli

item_format: derive intra-individual RT variability (SD and the slow-tail tau) and lapse frequency from any speeded block; per the worst-performance rule, a child's SLOWEST responses, not their fastest, carry the ability signal
cognitive_process: attentional control and consistency of processing (lapse regulation), not peak speed
engagement_affordance: design any speed game to log the full RT distribution; reward steadiness (few lapses) rather than a single fast burst, which also discourages reckless speed
adaptivity_fit: med - this is a scoring/analytics layer over existing speeded tasks rather than a new item; applies broadly
tail_discrimination: med - among speed indices, RT variability and worst-trial performance are the most ability-linked, so this is the best speed-derived tail signal (still modest)
coachability_bias_risk: harder to fake than peak speed (you cannot easily fake NOT lapsing); still affected by attention, fatigue, motivation and device latency
advantage_vs_cogat: this is the key insight for the construct: consistency/lapse metrics beat peak speed for ability and double as an engagement/effort check; CogAT yields no distributional/process data at all
source_name: Deary-Liewald reaction time task and the RT-variability/worst-performance literature (PsyToolkit)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - compute variability/tau/lapse metrics from our own speeded blocks

item_format: computer-administered same/not-same pattern comparison; raw score is the number of correct items completed in 90 seconds; distributed via the official HealthMeasures/NIH Toolbox program
cognitive_process: perceptual comparison speed (choice reaction time)
engagement_affordance: short, self-contained, and already child-tested (smiley/frowny for under-8s); wrap in a countdown but keep accuracy-first scoring
adaptivity_fit: high - standardized, brief, and continuously scored; easy to slot into a battery
tail_discrimination: low - purpose-built to isolate speed with minimized errors, so it does not stretch the gifted tail
coachability_bias_risk: documented practice effect; device/motor and attention confounds; motivation-sensitive
advantage_vs_cogat: weak standalone; a well-validated, free processing-speed index usable as collateral evidence and a consistency check; CogAT has no equivalent
source_name: NIH Toolbox (HealthMeasures)
reuse_note: describe_only - use the validated paradigm as a model; do not copy Toolbox items

item_format: scrolling digit-symbol substitution with keyboard or touch input; scores the number of correct matches and the average time per correct match
cognitive_process: perceptual matching speed with associative learning and response speed
engagement_affordance: the scrolling feed is intrinsically paced like a rhythm game; report correct count and average correct-match time, not frantic input
adaptivity_fit: high - key length, symbol set, input mode and duration are all configurable
tail_discrimination: low - a canonical speed measure; weak high-end separation
coachability_bias_risk: strong practice/memorization effects; input-device latency; attention-sensitive
advantage_vs_cogat: weak standalone; provides per-response timing (a consistency read) CogAT lacks; not a tail discriminator
source_name: Digit Symbol Substitution Test (Millisecond Test Library)
reuse_note: describe_only - the DSST paradigm is public but this specific Inquisit implementation is commercial; build our own

item_format: arcade tap-the-target with a visible accuracy meter: the combo builds only on correct AND fast taps and breaks on any false alarm, so speed is rewarded only when controlled
cognitive_process: visual search speed under an explicit speed-accuracy constraint
engagement_affordance: the reference design for gamifying speed responsibly - countdown and combo for excitement, but the false-alarm penalty prevents rewarding impulsive fast-but-wrong responding
adaptivity_fit: high - density, similarity and spawn rate scale difficulty; continuous scoring
tail_discrimination: low - even well-designed, arcade speed does not separate the gifted tail; use accuracy-gated speed and consistency as the real read
coachability_bias_risk: large practice/skill effects and device dependence remain; the accuracy gate mitigates (does not remove) impulsivity confounds
advantage_vs_cogat: weak as a gifted signal; its purpose is high, honest engagement plus an impulsivity/consistency read; CogAT offers no behavioral engagement telemetry
